Volume 16 · Chapter 07

Data construction, measurement and ethics

Research Author-reviewed · Prerequisites: v16-c06

By the endBuild a defensible research dataset with documented measurement and access constraints.

Build the dataset that the question actually requires

Capability. Construct a research dataset whose measurement, linkage, coverage and permitted use can be defended. The prerequisite is theory building and model discipline: a model's variable is not automatically a field in an administrative file. Use the target and counterfactual distinctions from question design, and the version discipline from reproduction. All records and study decisions below are original fictional teaching material. They contain no actual borrowers and authorize no real collection.

A bank's accounting system records what the bank needs to administer contracts. A research question may concern a borrower's total financing, the affordability of repayment or access to credit. Those objects differ. Even flawless code cannot turn a partial lender file into a complete credit history, or a self-reported late payment into a direct observation of every dimension of financial distress. Data construction is part of the argument connecting the economic concept to the reported result.

1. Specify measurement, collection and access together

Start with a measurement contract: target population; unit of observation; reference date or interval; economic concept; operational variable; units; source coverage; and missingness states. Define the grain, meaning what one row represents, and a key that distinguishes those rows. A loan-date table and a borrower-date table have different grains. Aggregating changes the grain; a join can multiply rows without creating new loans. Reconcile counts and monetary totals at each step.

A proxy is an observed measure used to learn about a concept that is not directly observed. Explain the mapping and its possible failures. A loan stock is not the flow of new advances: repayments, write-offs, sales and valuation changes can move the stock. Bank credit is not all financing if nonbank lenders are absent. A missed-payment report may reflect misunderstanding, recall or reporting incentives. Validate definitions against source documentation, transaction examples and, where permitted, independent measurements. Agreement between two files copied from the same source is not independent validation.

A collection plan specifies who produces each field, when, under which definitions, and how changes will be recorded. Before acquiring real records, establish the applicable access authority, permitted purpose, retention conditions and disclosure procedure. A researcher's ability to download a file does not determine the permitted use of its contents. For primary collection, pilot whether participants understand the questions and whether the recording process captures the intended event. For administrative data, inspect the institution's recording incentives and changes in its systems.

The AEA data and code policy inspected in Chapter 3 supplies a bounded professional reference for documenting provenance, transformations and the connection between code and outputs. Preserve raw snapshots and a transformation log. A hash identifies bytes; a dictionary explains their meaning. Neither establishes permission or factual accuracy by itself.

Record missingness separately from values. Useful states include observed amount, verified zero, missing report, unresolved linkage, outside the defined population and not applicable. Their consequences differ. A missing row can mean zero only if the recording contract and coverage establish that all relevant events would have been recorded. An absent institution's feed cannot supply that assurance. Retain reasons and denominators rather than collapsing all states to an empty cell.

2. Link entities without manufacturing observations

A crosswalk maps source identifiers to research entities. Names are evidence for a match, not necessarily identifiers. Record the source, effective dates and evidence behind a mapping. If an account code is reused or an entity merges, a timeless crosswalk can join the wrong units. Define whether a merger changes the target entity or is mapped into a stable perimeter. Do not let an automatic nearest-name rule silently settle an ambiguous economic identity.

Distinguish exact duplicate deliveries from conflicting records and legitimate repeated observations. An identical retransmission may be removed under a documented rule, retaining its audit count. Two different amounts for the same loan and date need a version or adjudication rule; keeping whichever row happens to come last is not a substantive resolution. Two different loans held by the same borrower should be summed, not deduplicated by borrower name. Test uniqueness at the original grain before changing that grain.

Worked case 1. A complete borrower-credit construction

Target and collection contract. Measure changes in outstanding credit from the fictional lenders N and S between dates 0 and 1 for the fixed baseline borrower roster B1,B2. Amounts in the analysis table are thousands of one fixed currency. The supplied source files contain loan-date balances, not new-credit flows. Borrower B3 appears later and is retained in the construction audit but excluded from the fixed baseline target. The two-lender universe excludes every other source of finance.

Complete delivered loan rows; the last two rows illustrate retransmission and missingness

L10Nn1thousand100
L20Ss7currency40000
L30Nn2thousand80
L11Nn1thousand90
L21Ss7currency60000
L41Ss9thousand20
L11Nn1thousand90
L31Nn2thousandNone

Completed dictionary. The original key is (lender,loan,date); account identifies the borrower within the lender. Dates are the two defined observation points, not retrieval times. Amount is a nonnegative integer or None; currency units become thousands by division by 1000. None means unavailable, not a closed loan. An identical repeated row is a retransmission. A different row with the same key is a conflict that stops this construction. These rules are stipulated for this teaching source, not universal properties of administrative data.

Completed linkage and coverage record. Verified fictional account documents map (N,n1)→B1, (S,s7)→B1, (N,n2)→B2 and (S,s9)→B3 throughout both dates. An earlier candidate crosswalk also mapped (N,n1) to B3; that candidate was rejected as ambiguous before analysis. The final unique mapping is the one shown. Coverage metadata says the complete N+S loan inventory is available for every borrower-date except B2 at date 1. For B3 at date 0, complete inventory and no loan rows establish zero. For B2 at date 1, missing coverage means its total remains unknown even if some constituent balances had been observed. Completeness is external metadata to audit; it is not inferred from a successful sum.

Completed analysis panel after unit conversion, linkage and audited deduplication
BorrowerDate 0Date 1Target and status
B1140150Baseline; both complete.
B280UnknownBaseline; date-1 coverage incomplete.
B3020Outside baseline roster; both complete.

The ingestion ledger is (8,7,1,6,5,1): eight delivered rows, seven unique loan-date rows, one exact retransmission removed, six borrower-date slots, five complete totals and one missing total. The fully observed baseline borrower B1 has change 10 and growth 1/14. That is not growth for the full baseline roster. Its initial total is 220; its final total is 150+x, where x is B2's unknown date-1 balance. Adding B3's20 would change the population. Setting x=0 without evidence would change a missing measurement into an asserted observation.

Executable construction. The complete program below embeds the exact raw rows, accepted crosswalk and coverage record. Copy it into construct.py and run python3 -I -B construct.py. It uses standard-library exact fractions, performs no file or network access, and prints the analysis panel and audit fields. It deliberately refuses ambiguous mappings, conflicting duplicates and a missing amount labeled complete. The program can enforce the supplied metadata; it cannot verify that an actual provider told the truth.

from fractions import Fraction as F
import json

RAW = (
    ("L1", 0, "N", "n1", "thousand", 100),
    ("L2", 0, "S", "s7", "currency", 40000),
    ("L3", 0, "N", "n2", "thousand", 80),
    ("L1", 1, "N", "n1", "thousand", 90),
    ("L2", 1, "S", "s7", "currency", 60000),
    ("L4", 1, "S", "s9", "thousand", 20),
    ("L1", 1, "N", "n1", "thousand", 90),
    ("L3", 1, "N", "n2", "thousand", None),
)
LINKS = (("N", "n1", "B1"), ("S", "s7", "B1"),
         ("N", "n2", "B2"), ("S", "s9", "B3"))
COVERAGE = {(b, t): not (b == "B2" and t == 1)
            for b in ("B1", "B2", "B3") for t in (0, 1)}
ROSTER = ("B1", "B2")

def construct(rows, links, coverage, roster):
    mapping = {}
    for lender, account, borrower in links:
        if not all(type(x) is str and x for x in (lender, account, borrower)):
            raise ValueError("nonempty identifiers required")
        if (lender, account) in mapping:
            raise ValueError("crosswalk key is not unique")
        mapping[lender, account] = borrower
    borrowers = set(mapping.values())
    slots = {(b, t) for b in borrowers for t in (0, 1)}
    if set(coverage) != slots or any(type(v) is not bool for v in coverage.values()):
        raise ValueError("complete boolean coverage map required")
    if not roster or len(set(roster)) != len(roster) or not set(roster) <= borrowers:
        raise ValueError("unique known target roster required")
    totals = {k: F(0) for k in slots}
    seen, duplicates = {}, 0
    for row in rows:
        if not isinstance(row, (tuple, list)) or len(row) != 6:
            raise ValueError("six fields per row required")
        loan, date, lender, account, unit, amount = row
        if not all(type(x) is str and x for x in (loan, lender, account)):
            raise ValueError("invalid record identifier")
        if type(date) is not int or date not in (0, 1):
            raise ValueError("date outside contract")
        if type(unit) is not str or unit not in ("currency", "thousand"):
            raise ValueError("unknown unit")
        if amount is not None and (type(amount) is not int or amount < 0):
            raise ValueError("nonnegative integer or None required")
        if (lender, account) not in mapping:
            raise ValueError("unresolved account linkage")
        key = (lender, loan, date)
        if key in seen:
            if seen[key] != tuple(row):
                raise ValueError("conflicting loan-date records")
            duplicates += 1
            continue
        seen[key] = tuple(row)
        slot = (mapping[lender, account], date)
        if amount is None:
            if coverage[slot]:
                raise ValueError("missing balance cannot be complete")
        else:
            totals[slot] += F(amount, 1000 if unit == "currency" else 1)
    panel = [[b, t, str(totals[b, t]) if coverage[b, t] else None,
              "complete" if coverage[b, t] else "missing"]
             for b, t in sorted(slots)]
    return {"baseline": list(roster), "duplicates_removed": duplicates,
            "panel": panel, "unique_loan_dates": len(seen)}

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(json.dumps(construct(RAW, LINKS, COVERAGE, ROSTER), sort_keys=True))

The actual executed output is:

{"baseline": ["B1", "B2"], "duplicates_removed": 1, "panel": [["B1", 0, "140", "complete"], ["B1", 1, "150", "complete"], ["B2", 0, "80", "complete"], ["B2", 1, null, "missing"], ["B3", 0, "0", "complete"], ["B3", 1, "20", "complete"]], "unique_loan_dates": 7}

Completed release note. “Version teaching-1 contains the complete supplied raw input, dictionary, unique crosswalk, coverage map, fixed target roster, program and audit output. The exact retransmission was removed; the ambiguous candidate mapping was rejected. B1's growth is observed, whereas the baseline aggregate is unavailable without B2's missing balance or explicit restrictions. No causal effect, comprehensive financing measure or real empirical fact is claimed. Next obtain authorized evidence about B2's coverage, preserving the original missing state and any revised vintage.”

3. Treat access, consent and disclosure as design questions

Privacy concerns what information about people or organizations can be exposed and used. Confidentiality concerns how entrusted information is handled. Replacing a name with a code does not necessarily remove the ability to connect a row to its subject. Linkage keys and rare attribute combinations may remain informative. The abstract of NIST SP800-188 (2023) emphasizes evaluating disclosure risk and choosing a sharing model; it warns that masking personal information alone may be insufficient. This is a bounded reference to that abstract, not a claim to have implemented its full technical guidance.

The 1979 Belmont Report provides an ethical framework of respect for persons, beneficence and justice. Its consent discussion distinguishes information, understanding and voluntary choice. Applied here, consent is a process to evaluate, not merely a signature field. These principles do not determine every current legal or institutional requirement. For an actual project, obtain the applicable determination about review, access and consent arrangements before using records; neither a lender's cooperation nor this chapter supplies it.

Minimize the information needed for the question. Separate linkage material from analysis variables, define who can access each, and specify the permitted outputs and retention end point. A deletion promise must be compatible with the actual research and archive arrangements; do not promise withdrawal from an already published aggregate if that cannot be implemented. Access to administrative data and agreement to answer a survey are distinct matters. State whether linkage is proposed and what declining would mean.

Research integrity also concerns the analysis record. Preserve exclusions, match adjudications, definition changes and unexplained discrepancies. Correct errors visibly, identifying affected outputs. Do not fabricate an unobserved outcome, silently change a target to improve a result, or describe an unperformed check as completed. An unresolved conflict can justify postponing analysis or narrowing the claim. It need not be concealed to preserve a useful project.

Worked case 2. A completed access and missingness decision

Proposed study. A fictional team wants to relate credit records to borrower hardship. It proposes an optional survey asking whether a payment was late during a specified month. The operational outcome is a self-reported late-payment indicator, not a complete measure of hardship. The eligible roster has (100,60,48,18):100 eligible borrowers,60 who agree to the proposed survey and linkage,48 with usable responses,18 reporting a late payment. These are stipulated counts from a hypothetical teaching scenario, not an actual collection or authorization.

Completed decisions before a real version could proceed
IssueDecision, owner and evidence required
Purpose and accessThe research lead documents the narrow question, administrative fields, linkage purpose and intended outputs. The institution's authorized process determines whether the proposed access and consent arrangements are permissible. Stop acquisition until that determination and the provider's permitted-use terms are documented.
Voluntary participationA researcher independent of lending decisions explains participation and linkage separately from loan servicing. The proposed script states that declining will not affect credit decisions; the team must verify it can honor that promise. Use a comprehension check about linkage and declining. A loan officer's pressure cannot be repaired by collecting a signature.
Collection and linkageCollect only fields needed for the specified month and question. A designated linkage custodian maintains the identity crosswalk under the approved access plan. Analysts receive project codes and required variables, not contact details. Record match uncertainty; do not expose extra identifiers merely to maximize the match rate.
ReleaseDo not publicly release linked borrower rows on the assumption that coded names are anonymous. Submit proposed tables and accompanying information to the designated disclosure review. Until a release is approved, provide original fictional demonstration data and permitted code/documentation. Fictional examples do not establish that a model trained on confidential data would be safe to release.
Retention and incident responseThe data custodian records the approved storage locations, access log, retention dates and disposition procedure. The research lead records whom to notify and how to contain an unauthorized disclosure under the applicable institutional process. No invented universal retention period or legal reporting deadline is supplied.
Selection and reportingThe analysis lead preserves the eligible, consenting and responding denominators. Report response coverage and missingness sensitivity. Do not contact nonconsenters to collect prohibited outcomes merely to make the dataset complete. If a population claim cannot be supported, narrow it and retain the limitation.

A concrete disclosure failure. Suppose a proposed coded row contains a small town, exact age54 and a rare occupation, and an accessible directory has exactly one person with that combination. Removing the name does not prevent a link to the row's payment response. This original hypothetical example establishes a possible failure of name masking; it does not measure an actual re-identification probability. Generalizing ages or suppressing fields may change both risk and statistical usefulness. Evaluate the complete release and plausible auxiliary information, including earlier releases, rather than declaring any one transformation universally safe.

Completed missingness analysis. The response rate among those who agreed is 4/5. The observed late-payment fraction is 3/8. For the60 consenting borrowers, the12 missing indicators may each be0 or1. The fraction is therefore between18/60 and30/60: (3/10,1/2). For the100 eligible borrowers,52 indicators are unobserved; the compatible fraction is between18/100 and70/100: (9/50,7/10). These are finite-roster logical bounds for the specified binary response if it were defined for every target member. They do not establish true hardship rates, sampling confidence coverage or a causal effect. The binary measurement definition itself requires scrutiny.

The bounds are sharp under only the stated binary restriction: setting every unobserved indicator to0 attains the lower endpoint, and setting every one to1 attains the upper endpoint. Every integer count between is attainable, so the feasible rates form a finite grid within each displayed interval; no claim that arbitrary real-valued rates between grid points occur in a fixed finite roster is needed. The complete-case fraction3/8 need not equal either target fraction. More accurate arithmetic does not resolve nonresponse or consent selection.

Completed project decision. “Proceed only after the actual access/review determination, a credible voluntary recruitment process and approved linkage/output arrangements exist. Our descriptive result would concern reported late payment among respondents. For broader rosters, show the stated logical bounds and justify any stronger missingness assumptions separately. We will not present nonparticipation as zero hardship, force participation for statistical convenience, or publish coded microdata without disclosure review. If permitted linkage is unavailable, a nonlinked descriptive survey may be considered under a revised contract; it cannot answer the original linked-record question.”

4. Exercises

  1. Write a measurement contract for case1 specifying both grains, keys, target roster, credit universe, units, dates and the distinction between a missing value and verified zero. Name two economic questions that the constructed balances cannot answer alone.
  2. If the identical retransmission is not removed, compute B1's date-1 total and growth. Separately, suppose the N,n1 crosswalk row is accidentally duplicated with the same B1 destination, expanding every matching loan-date row after correct raw deduplication. Compute B1's totals and growth in this second error. Explain why neither change is real credit creation.
  3. For case1, suppose defensible external information bounds B2's missing date-1 balance by0≤x≤160 thousand. Derive the sharp interval for growth of the fixed baseline total. Exhibit one compatible negative-growth and one positive-growth completion. Explain why B1's positive growth does not identify the aggregate sign.
  4. A provider now supplies a verified closed-loan record for B2 and complete coverage showing no other N/S credit at date1. What changes in the program inputs and target result? Contrast that revision with merely replacing None by0 while keeping coverage incomplete. State how the revision should be documented.
  5. Recompute case2's response rate, complete-case late-payment rate and both target-roster bounds if usable responses increase from48 to50 and late-payment reports from18 to19, with the other counts unchanged. Give the full possible integer-count ranges and distinguish logical bounds from confidence intervals.
  6. A colleague wants to label the survey outcome “financial distress,” omit nonconsenters from the reported denominator, and publicly share rows after replacing names with hashes. Write a constructive correction addressing measurement, selection and disclosure. Do not assert that a hash makes the file anonymous or that an arbitrary suppression threshold guarantees safety.
  7. Draft a short, plain-language explanation for the proposed optional survey/linkage that addresses purpose, requested information, linkage, possible risks, declining, questions and limits on withdrawal. Then state what must be verified before the team can use it. This is a teaching draft, not an approved consent form.
  8. Produce a complete release-and-correction memo for case1 after discovering that an earlier result counted the retransmission. Include the affected target, old/new number, root cause, preserved inputs/code versions, checks, remaining missingness and the honest claim. Add what would change if the records were confidential rather than entirely fictional.
Complete solutions and evaluation criteria

1. Define what a row and zero mean

Source grain is loan-date within lender, keyed by(lender,loan,date); analysis grain is borrower-date, keyed by(borrower,date). The fixed target roster is B1,B2; credit includes N and S only; the balance unit is thousands of the same currency at dates0 and1. An observed zero requires reliable coverage and evidence of no balance. B2's incomplete date1 remains unknown, whereas B3's complete empty date0 inventory establishes zero. Balances alone do not measure new advances, credit supply effects, total finance across excluded lenders, investment or welfare. Full credit supplies every requested contract component and two explicit limits, rather than a generic statement that data may be imperfect.

2. Diagnose two different multiplications

Keeping the retransmission adds90 to B1's correct150, yielding240; with initial140 its growth is (240,5/7). The duplicated crosswalk instead doubles the N component at both dates after raw deduplication: initial2(100)+40=240 and final2(90)+60=240, giving (240,240,0). The first repeats a delivered observation; the second repeats matches during a join. No borrower acquired another loan because a row appeared twice. Check the key and reconcile totals at both stages; deduplicating only the final borrower table would discard legitimate loans or fail to recover the correct sums.

3. Preserve the unknown component

Baseline initial credit is220 and final credit150+x, so growth=(x−70)/220. Its sharp continuous-balance interval is (-7/22,9/22), with endpoints at x=0 and160. If raw balances are restricted to integer currency units, feasible rates instead lie on the corresponding fine grid with the same endpoints. Choosing x=0 yields−7/22; choosing x=100 yields3/22, so opposite aggregate signs fit the observed B1 growth. Every allowed x preserves the known records, making the bound constructive. The interval is conditional on the extra upper bound, not a confidence interval or a consequence of the program.

4. Distinguish evidence from imputation

In a new documented vintage, change B2's date1 amount to0 and its coverage flag to complete, retaining the old inputs. The panel then reports observed zero. Baseline final credit150 gives growth -7/22. If only the amount is changed while coverage remains incomplete, the program still reports a missing borrower total: another unobserved loan could exist within the declared universe. The new closed-loan and coverage evidence—not the numeric substitution—justifies zero. Record provider/version/date, affected fields, evidence, old/new output and tests; do not erase the earlier missing-data result.

5. Update each denominator separately

The response rate is50/60=5/6; the observed rate is 19/50. Consenting borrowers have10 unobserved outcomes, so the possible positive counts are every integer19 through29, giving (19/60,29/60). Eligible borrowers have50 unobserved outcomes, so counts run through69 and the bounds are (19/100,69/100). These are sharp logical count ranges given the binary definition, not probability statements or coverage-calibrated intervals. Neither the increased response rate nor a narrower bound proves that late payment captures all hardship.

6. Correct the claim at three distinct boundaries

“Call the measured variable a reported late payment in the specified month; explain why it is a proxy and what aspects of distress it misses. Keep the eligible, consenting and responding counts visible, and label the complete-case rate and broader bounds separately. Hashing names changes an identifier but does not remove information in other fields or establish an approved release. Review the proposed outputs, access controls and auxiliary information with the designated process; share only approved material. Original fictional demonstrations can illustrate the code while the actual release remains unresolved.” Full credit addresses all three issues and gives a usable revision. It must not invent a universal safe cell size, prove voluntariness from a signature, or treat unavailable records as observed negatives.

7. A draft explanation whose promises need verification

“We are studying how reported payment difficulties relate to credit records during the specified month. We would ask whether a payment was late and, if you agree to the proposed linkage, connect your answers to the described N/S credit fields using a separately protected identity record. Disclosure could expose sensitive financial information; the project plans restricted access and reviewed outputs but cannot promise that risk is zero. Taking part is optional, and declining will not affect lending decisions. You may ask the research team questions before deciding. The team will explain the actual withdrawal deadline and what can still be removed before you agree; it will not promise to undo a public aggregate already released.” Before use, verify the real study facts, institutional determination, permitted linkage, independence from lending decisions, access/release controls, contact route, language/comprehension arrangements and feasible withdrawal terms. Full credit addresses all requested topics and separates a teaching draft from approved operational language; it need not copy these sentences.

8. A complete correction memo

“The earlier B1 matched-balance result used a retransmitted L1 date1 row twice. B1 date1 was reported as240 and growth as5/7; corrected deduplication gives150 and1/14. The fixed baseline aggregate was never identified from the incomplete B2 record and must not be inferred from either B1 number. We retained the original delivery and code, created a corrected version with the exact-key/identical-payload rule, and recorded eight delivered rows, seven unique loan-date records and one removed retransmission. We checked the unique crosswalk, unit conversion, complete/missing flags, final panel and independently recomputed totals. The remaining descriptive claim is B1's observed growth within N/S credit; B2 remains missing and no causal claim follows.” If records were confidential, corrections would use the authorized audience and disclosure process; preserve the audit trail in approved storage and release only permitted outputs. Full credit includes the old/new numbers, cause, versions, verification and residual claim boundary, not merely an apology.

5. Teach-back and delayed retention

Teach-back. Explain why a dataset can have unique keys and no code errors yet fail the economic question or ethical access contract. Use one measurement example and one access or disclosure example from this chapter.

Answer guide

A perfectly keyed N/S loan panel remains incomplete for total financing outside those lenders; a missing B2 total cannot become observed through a clean join. Separately, coded survey rows may remain linkable through rare attributes, and a functioning linkage program does not establish permitted use. Correct computation, appropriate measurement and authorized handling require separate evidence.

Delayed retention. A week later, a provider supplies a new crosswalk and asks you to overwrite the old one. Design a response that preserves reproducibility and tests whether the target population or measurements change.

Criteria and illustrative response

Preserve both versions, document the source/date/reason and effective periods, compare changed mappings, test key uniqueness and unresolved links, and rebuild the same frozen raw snapshot under each mapping. Reconcile borrower counts and balances and inspect whether a merger, corrected identity or reused code changes the target perimeter. Record affected outputs and justify any revised population. Verify permitted handling of both crosswalks; do not publish identifying material merely to show the comparison. A new hash alone does not explain what the mapping changes mean.

Next step. Carry the measurement contract, feasible access plan and unresolved missingness into research design, power and preregistration. Plan a study around data that can actually answer its target, and record in advance what evidence would require a pivot.

Sources and further study

  • American Economic Association — Data and Code Availability Policy (page labeled February2026) — Narrow professional benchmark for documented provenance, transformations, analysis and output mapping.
  • NIST SP800-188 — De-Identifying Government Datasets: Techniques and Governance (September2023), abstract/publication record — Narrow disclosure-risk/sharing-model framing and warning that masking alone may be insufficient.
  • The Belmont Report — Ethical Principles and Guidelines for Protection of Human Subjects of Research (18April1979), HHS/OHRP text — Bounded historical ethical principles and consent concepts.
